title: Ship signed and notarized macOS app/DMG (repaired: delegate to RightKit)
notes: This is a repair of the prior MBR-901 pass, which landed at commit 2d543114 ('MBR-901: ship signed and notarized macOS app/DMG') with a bespoke codesign/notarytool/stapler pipeline: packaging/macos/bundle-manifest.json + release-contract.json describing a hand-rolled inner-to-outer signing order, and scripts/release/macos/{contract,release-macos}.mjs's validateBundleManifest/signingOrder plus `sign`/`notarize`/`staple`/`plan` CLI commands that shelled out to codesign/xcrun notarytool/xcrun stapler directly. Adrian clarified afterward that RightKit already provides proper signing on both macOS and Windows and is already wired into apps/membrane-hub: right-release.config.mjs's targets.mac declares signed:true, package: `pnpm run rightkit:package:mac` (apps/membrane-hub/scripts/build-mac-release.mjs, which already runs `tauri build --bundles app,dmg`, `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, `xcrun stapler staple`/`validate`, and `spctl -a -vv` on the DMG), and installer/hardening keys pointing at the built DMG. The prior pass duplicated all of that instead of delegating to it -- including inventing its own credential env-var names (MEMBRANE_MACOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY, MEMBRANE_MACOS_NOTARY_PROFILE) that nothing in the real build ever read.

This task deletes the duplication and keeps only two layers: (a) acceptance/verification of RightKit's real output, and (b) the one piece of evidence RightKit's build genuinely does not persist. packaging/macos/release-contract.json and packaging/macos/bundle-manifest.json are deleted outright -- no code in this repository computes a signing order anymore, because RightKit's own build (via Tauri) already codesigns crypt-service, the membrane sidecar, and Membrane Hub.app inner-to-outer with hardened runtime, using the identity in apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json. scripts/release/macos/contract.mjs dropped validateReleaseContract/validateBundleManifest/signingOrder/SIGNING_IDENTITY_ENV/NOTARY_PROFILE_ENV entirely. It keeps buildPlatformAcceptanceReceipt/validatePlatformAcceptanceReceipt unchanged (this is membrane's own book-gate evidence type, reusing scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs -- RightKit has no equivalent, since it seals build artifacts but does not attest install/update lifecycle outcomes). It adds readSealedReleaseManifest/verifySealedInstallerHash/sealedReleaseDir, which read back RightKit's real .right-release/sealed/<app>-<version>-<commit8>/mac/release-manifest.json so the acceptance layer verifies RightKit's actual sealed artifact by hash, not an arbitrary same-named file. It adds a notarytoolAuthArgs() that mirrors (cannot import -- see below) @rightkit/release/notary-auth.mjs's function of the same name, so notarization-log capture authenticates exactly like the real build did, replacing the prior pass's disconnected env-var names with the ones the real build actually reads (the apple-dev-notary keychain profile, or APPLE_API_KEY_PATH/APPLE_API_KEY/APPLE_API_ISSUER).

scripts/release/macos/release-macos.mjs deleted the `sign`, `notarize`, `staple`, and `plan` commands -- each duplicated an action RightKit/Tauri already performs. `verify` was rewritten to run only read-only checks against RightKit's already-built artifacts: codesign --verify --deep --strict, the hardened-runtime flag check, spctl --assess on the .app, hdiutil verify + spctl --assess on the DMG, and (newly folded in, since it is a read, not a mutation) xcrun stapler validate on both the .app and the DMG. A new optional --sealed-dir flag cross-checks the --dmg bytes against RightKit's sealed release-manifest.json hash. `receipt` reuses that same read-only check suite instead of a bespoke sign+notarize+staple sequence, but keeps its prior orthic.membrane.macos-release-receipt.v1 output shape unchanged (confirmed: this schema is only referenced within this task's own files, not by any downstream consumer). `verify-receipt` and `platform-receipt` are functionally unchanged -- platform-receipt in particular still builds the exact orthic.membrane.platform-acceptance.v1 receipt scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs, scripts/release/verify-release-evidence.mjs, and downstream MBR-904/MBR-808 already consume, so nothing downstream breaks. `notarization-log` is the one genuinely missing piece kept and rewritten: RightKit's build script submits and waits for notarization but never persists the submission ID or a durable log file anywhere, so this command runs `xcrun notarytool log <submission-id>` and writes it to a confined, non-overwritable path -- this is the notarization-log evidence MBR-901's acceptance criterion names, and nothing in RightKit currently produces it.

packaging/macos/entitlements.plist is kept, not deleted: its empty <dict/> already grants no exceptions, which is behaviorally identical to Tauri's default when no entitlements file is configured (apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json#bundle.macOS.entitlements is unset). Its header comment was rewritten to say so honestly -- it is a rationale document today, not a wired build input, since wiring it in touches apps/membrane-hub/** (a concurrent lane, out of scope for this task).

Genuinely missing from RightKit and kept in this pipeline, with reasons: (1) notarization-log capture -- RightKit's build submits and waits but does not persist the submission ID/log; (2) the notarytoolAuthArgs() mirror -- this membrane repository is its own standalone Git checkout with no workspace/file link to tools/rightkit (RightKit's own rules forbid apps depending on it by anything but a published npm version), and the membrane repo root has no @rightkit/release dependency at all (only apps/membrane-hub does, for its own build script), so the ~15-line, non-signing, credential-argument-shape helper could not be imported across that boundary and was mirrored instead, with its default profile name and env-var names now matching what the real build reads, replacing the prior pass's disconnected names; (3) the whole read-only `verify`/`receipt` check suite -- this is acceptance/QA evidence-gathering over RightKit's output, not a build step RightKit performs, and MBR-901's acceptance criterion explicitly names each of these checks. Nothing else was added.

Per this task's hard rules, no cargo/pnpm/Tauri build, right-release, codesign, notarytool, spctl, stapler, or any other signing command was run. The only command executed was `node --test scripts/release/macos/release-macos-pipeline.test.mjs` -- see commands.log. No mutating git command was run; this evidence bundle and the source files above are uncommitted, for the orchestrator to squash into the existing MBR-901 history per this task's instructions.

Files outside this task's allowlist that this task needed to read (not modify) to understand what RightKit already does: apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs, apps/membrane-hub/package.json, apps/membrane-hub/scripts/build-mac-release.mjs, apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json, tools/rightkit/packages/release/{cli/right-release.mjs,build-release.mjs,release.mjs,release-state.mjs,notary-auth.mjs,hardeningscan.mjs,create-mac-updater.mjs}, and scripts/release/windows/{contract.mjs,verify-receipt.mjs} (read only, for pattern parity; no windows file was modified).
